notes: A one-bullet quest and the bullet really is the whole quest: the trade both starts and finishes it, so there is no separate 'talk to accept' step to add. The Description writes the items as 'a Sheet of Parchment and a Jar of Black Ink', which are the flavour phrasings; the walkthrough and Item Reqs both use the real inventory names Parchment and Black Ink, and those are what resolve (917 and 929). The Reward is a Mog House exit privilege, not an item, so there is nothing observable anywhere in this quest and evidence is null -- correct rather than reached for.

Two bullets, two steps, one NPC -- talk then trade, both on Oswald, so the runtime draws a single marker and reads readiness ahead across them. The sub-bullet under [1] ('The Sand Charm must be completed before being offered this quest') is a precondition, not an action, and it is already carried by the header's Previous list, which names both The Gift and The Sand Charm; that is why it costs nothing here where the same sentence had to be flagged on The Gift. Fame reads 'Other', which is not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept. The Glass Fiber F. Rod is the Reward and therefore not evidence.

steps.note: he only offers this once The Sand Charm is complete

notes: There is no ladder here to build. The entire walkthrough is one bullet -- 'This quest is triggered automatically after completing Tenuous Existence' -- which describes something that happens TO the player, not something the player does. It does not say what completes the quest either, so the page is truncated as well as actionless. The header's giver, Joachim in Port Jeuno, is never mentioned in the walkthrough at all; I have kept him verbatim in start because he is the only place the page offers, and set confidence low precisely so the emitter falls back to a start-NPC marker on him instead of trusting a one-rung ladder I would have had to invent. The single step recorded is the auto-trigger itself: kind cutscene, target none, so it can never place a marker and can never claim a hand-in that the page does not describe. Fame 'Abyssea' is not one of the nine regions and resolves to nothing, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept. VERIFY: the draft carried Port Jeuno down onto the step from the header; the walkthrough places the auto-trigger nowhere, so the step's zone is nulled. start keeps Joachim/Port Jeuno verbatim, which is where the header's claim belongs.

steps.note: the quest flags itself on completing Tenuous Existence; there is nothing for the player to do and the page names no target, so this rung is deliberately unmarkable. The walkthrough gives no location at all -- Port Jeuno is only where the header puts Joachim, who is never mentioned in the walkthrough -- so the zone is left null rather than asserting the auto-trigger happens there.

notes: The only interesting thing on this page is the OR. The walkthrough says 'five pieces of the same type of onion equipment' -- five of ONE type, not five assorted -- and the header spells the five types out. That is exactly what items / items_alt are for: items is the Onion Dagger x5 branch and the other four x5 branches sit in items_alt, each one independently sufficient. Writing all five into items would have made an AND-list demanding twenty-five onion weapons. All five resolve (16482, 16483, 17068, 17104, 16534), so items_partial is false: there is no branch left unexpressed. Romeo's grid is not given anywhere on the page, so it stays null rather than being guessed from Selbina's map. The Wastebasket is the Reward and is not evidence.

steps.note: five of the SAME type; the five types are alternatives to one another, not a shopping list

notes: Steps 1 and 3 are both Foss, and step 2 is deliberately wedged between them: bullet 2 is a real top-level instruction ('obtain 5 Rusty Buckets by either fishing for them or buying them...'), not acquisition trivia, and it sends you out of Bastok Markets entirely. It is the one rung in this quest that anything can be observed on, so it carries the evidence -- five Rusty Buckets -- and the trade below it carries the same five as its requirement. It has no zone: fishing, an auction house and Kahah Hobichai in Al Zahbi are three different places and a step has one zone. Kahah Hobichai is a vendor named in passing, not a target, so he stays in the note. The 300 gil reward is not observable.

steps.note: fish them up, buy them off an auction house, or buy them from Kahah Hobichai in Al Zahbi; the page names no fishing spot, so no zone is recorded

notes:
The trap on this page is that the hairpin does NOT go to the quest giver. Bullet 1 names Qiji, his wife and the item in one sentence, and a verb-scanner would happily trade to Qiji; bullet 3 says plainly to trade it to Romilda, and Qiji is only talked to again afterwards for the reward. Three steps: Qiji, Romilda, Qiji.

Bullet 2 is NOT a step. 'Brass hairpins can be bought off auction houses, or by crafting one' is a statement about where the item exists, with no instruction in it -- unlike Buckets of Gold in this same batch, which says 'obtain 5 Rusty Buckets' outright and therefore does get an obtain rung. Nothing is lost by folding it into a note: step 2's items already make holding the hairpin the readiness test.

Romilda has no grid of her own anywhere on the page; bullet 3 says she is 'standing next to Qiji' and the header puts Qiji at (I-7), so that is the grid she gets, flagged as inferred.

steps.note: he asks for a Brass Hairpin for his wife Romilda; buy one off an auction house or craft it (bullet 2, which is not itself a step)
the wife, not Qiji. The grid is Qiji's, because the page only says she stands next to him.

notes:
The ladder is simple and I am confident in it; the demotion to medium is entirely about the gate. Quest Reqs is 'Cook's Pride quest active' -- ACTIVE, not complete -- and gates.prev means completed. Putting Cook's Pride in prev would gate this quest on the exact state that makes it unavailable, so prev is left empty and the requirement is recorded here instead. Previous is empty on the page, so nothing is being dropped.

Bullet 1's sub-bullet is the only pointer to a source: Death Jackets by the main entrance of Crawler's Nest. That is enough to give the obtain step a zone and a mob with role drop, which is a real marker where the page would otherwise give none -- and note the zone resolves as 'Crawler's Nest' without an article, unlike The Eldieme Necropolis. Royal Jelly is also an auction-house item, but the page does not say so, so nothing is invented.

The Super soup pot key item is the header's Reward. It proves the quest is over, not that a rung is done, so it is not used as evidence even though it would otherwise be the cleanest observable in the quest.

steps.note: the sub-bullet says Death Jackets are prevalent and easily reached from the main entrance of Crawler's Nest, which is where the zone and the mob come from
the Super soup pot key item comes back from this trade, but it is the Reward, so it is not evidence

notes: Same shape as The Real Gift -- talk to Oswald, trade Oswald -- and I am confident in both rungs; the medium is the gate again. Quest Reqs says 'Must have started the quest The Sand Charm', and started is not finished, so The Sand Charm cannot go in prev without gating this quest on a state the page does not require. Previous names Under the Sea, which is a completed prerequisite and is modelled. The sub-bullet under [2] is auction-house advice for the Danceshroom, not a step, and there is no obtain rung because the trade's items already make holding one the readiness test. The Sleep Dagger is the Reward and is not evidence; nothing in this quest is observable before the hand-in, so both steps carry null.

steps.note: The Sand Charm must already be started for him to offer this
the sub-bullet is auction-house advice, not a rung

notes:
The walkthrough is a single unnumbered sentence rather than a bulleted list, so there is no [1] to cite; the one step is recorded against source_bullets [1] by convention and the shape is flagged so the audit trail is not misread as a numbered bullet that went missing.

The giver is not an NPC: it is the Cermet Headstone at Yuhtunga Jungle (L-7), a clickable object, and the whole quest is one trade to it. That is unusual but correct -- the header and the walkthrough agree on it exactly, so there is no start_disagrees_with_header here, only a start that happens to be furniture.

Medium is for the gate. Quest Reqs is 'Zilart Mission 5 - Headstone Pilgrimage Active or Complete', and 'active or complete' is a disjunction gates.prev cannot express -- prev means completed, which would hide the quest from exactly the players doing it during Mission 5, the case the sentence 'at any time during or after' goes out of its way to allow. Previous is empty, so nothing is dropped by leaving prev empty. The Opo-opo Necklace is the Reward, so it is not evidence, which leaves this quest with nothing observable at all.

steps.note: any time during or after Zilart Mission 5; the Opo-opo Necklace comes straight back but is the Reward, not evidence

notes:
Bullet 2 is four steps, not one. It names four grid refs in one zone and says only 'click on the signposts at the following spots' -- no order is stated or implied -- so the four examines share a group and are drawn all at once. A strict ladder would mark (E-11) and nothing else until you happened to walk to it, which is the failure this schema's groups exist to avoid, and unlike An Explorer's Footsteps these are four rungs in one zone so nothing is lost by splitting them out.

The page only ever writes 'the signposts', plural and lowercase. I have recorded the target as the singular Signpost, which is a normalisation of a name that is on the page rather than an invention of one, and flagged it: if the live entity turns out to be called something else these four rungs keep their places and lose only their markers. Nothing here is observable -- cleaning a signpost grants no item and no key item -- so all six steps carry null evidence and the ladder relies on the session latch between Maugie and Maugie. The 1,500 gil reward is not observable either.

Bullet 2's 'Travel to Jugner Forest' is not a separate travel rung: it is how you get to the four examines, and each of them already carries Jugner Forest as its zone.

steps.note: first of four, in any order
last of the four; all four must be cleaned before Maugie pays
